name: remember-and-recall: the Subconscious, Intuition seat
description: Keeps what a person knows as cards and recalls the ones that bear on the task at hand, from the asker's own scope: the cards a context assembler names for the query, then the cards the store finds by its words.
purpose: Give an AI the context a task needs and nothing from another person's scope.
approach: Store knowledge as cards and admit it by relevance within the scope of the asker.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-remember-and-recall has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-remember-and-recall has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-remember-and-recall chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Right context admitted, nothing from another scope.
outputs: The cards a task needs, in one rendered view with their ids.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: context-assembler: pick the context a task needs
description: Selects the context a task needs from a store and renders it into one view, together with the ids of the cards it drew on.
purpose: Find the passages that bear on a request, for any consumer that keeps knowledge to draw on.
approach: Rank stored documents against the request by keywords, meaning or both, and return the top results.
milestones: BM25, vector, hybrid and composite arms with recorded runs on public retrieval sets.
knowledge: Retrieval quality depends on the corpus, so arms are compared on the same public and written queries.
measures_of_success: A relevant document is among the first five results.
parameters: The store and optional model provider the arm is built with, and the number of hits.
outputs: An assembled context view and the ids of the cards it drew on; it never raises.
usage_notes: Pass root= for the folder to index. With no root the corpus is empty and nothing is returned.

name: cards-from-files: cards for a folder
description: Proposes a proportionate, current set of cards for material a consumer already keeps in files, without writing them.
purpose: Give any consumer cards for the knowledge it already keeps in files, so recall starts from what is there instead of an empty store.
approach: Group the files that belong together, describe each group, and report which cards an edit has made stale.
out_of_scope: Writing cards (the card store does) and choosing which cards a task sees (the context assembler does).
milestones: 1. The selected builder's balanced score on the pinned topic cases is at least that of every free topic builder, with its store under the cap of 0.25 cards per file (metric-cards-topic-needs). The file-finding and orientation metrics are floors and proxies and never select.
knowledge: Code graphs and repository maps group code by its call and import structure without a model; topic cards a model writes add the names a person would search for. A card groups information on one topic from many files and sources; a card per file is an index of files, so per_file_symbols and the degenerate groupings are baselines for file finding and never builders to ship. The earlier selection of per_file_symbols came from the file-finding metric, whose cases have one needed file each and so favour a card per file by construction; that metric was ill-posed for this solution, and the selection is back on llm_topic_cards until metric-cards-topic-needs decides.
measures_of_success: The files a piece of work needed are inside the first cards the fixed selector picks, with little noise and with files of more than one folder bundled when the task spans them, from a store of at most 0.25 cards per file, at a price per build a team would pay.
parameters: The model provider, for a builder that calls one.
inputs: A folder root, the list of files to read, and the cards already kept for it.
outputs: Cards in the card-store record shape (grouping, summary, keywords, files with their hashes), and the ids of kept cards whose files changed.
effects: Reads files; writes nothing (the caller writes through card-store).
usage_notes: Run it for a first index and after edits, passing the cards already kept so a builder skips covered files. The per-file builder is the free floor; a builder that calls a model has to buy its price in accuracy on the balanced score. The per-file builder is a baseline for finding one file, not a card builder. The free topic builders (cochange_topic_cards, import_graph_topic_cards, the replay of the saved paid build) are scored for free; docs/how-to/iterate-on-card-builders-without-repeating-model-calls.md says how to iterate before any paid run.
